rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Fungi are a distinct kingdom of eukaryotic, heterotrophic organisms with chitin cell walls and absorptive nutrition. They are classified into four major groups — Phycomycetes (lower, aseptate), Ascomycetes (sac fungi), Basidiomycetes (club fungi), and Deuteromycetes (imperfect).…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Fungi have a chitin cell wall (like arthropods), NOT cellulose (like plants).  ·  Fungi are NOT plants: they are heterotrophic, lack chlorophyll, and are in a separate kingdom.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB frequently asks for a labelled diagram of Penicillium (conidiophore, conidia, sterigmata).  ·  Memorise the four fungal groups with one example each and their spore type.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Penicillium notatum → antibiotic penicillin (Ascomycete).  ·  Saccharomyces cerevisiae → yeast for bread, beer, wine (Ascomycete).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Deuteromycetes are "imperfect" fungi — they have lost the sexual stage; they are not a true phylogenetic group.  ·  Yeast (Saccharomyces) is an Ascomycete; it reproduces by budding (asexual) but also by forming ascospores.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Draw Penicillium (labelled)  ·  Tabulate 4 fungal groups

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Fungi = F-H-C (Heterotrophic, Chitin wall) — remember "Fungi Hates Cellulose".  ·  Asco = sac; Basidio = club; Deutero = imperfect.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Why are fungi placed in a separate kingdom rather than with plants?  ·  Differentiate Phycomycetes from Deuteromycetes (4 points).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Draw and label Penicillium (conidiophore, conidia, sterigmata) — very common.  ·  Tabulate four fungal groups (spore, example, use).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Four fungal groups  ·  Chitin cell wall  ·  Mycelium & hyphae  ·  Asci vs basidia

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Fungi are eukaryotic, heterotrophic, chitin cell wall, no chloroplasts.  ·  Four groups: Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes.  ·  Body = mycelium (hyphae); reproduction = asexual (spores/budding) + sexual.  ·  Ascomycetes → asci; Basidiomycetes → basidia.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Penicillin, discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928, is produced by the fungus Penicillium chrysogenum.  ·  Mycorrhizal fungi form mutualistic associations with ~90% of land plants, aiding phosphorus uptake.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the structure of a Penicillium conidiophore.  ·  Explain the role of fungi in the decomposition cycle.  ·  What is the significance of the chitin cell wall in fungi?

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain why fungi are not plants.  ·  Describe the economic importance of fungi (5 points).

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Agaricus bisporus → edible mushroom (Basidiomycete).  ·  Rhizopus stolonifer → bread mould (Phycomycete).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The cell wall of fungi is made of: → B  ·  Penicillium belongs to which fungal group? → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Fungi: eukaryotic, heterotrophic (absorptive nutrition), cell wall of chitin, no chloroplasts; include moulds, yeasts, mushrooms.  ·  Four major groups: Phycomycetes (lower fungi, e.g. Rhizopus, water moulds), Ascomycetes (sac fungi, e.g. Penicillium, yeast, morels), Basidiomycetes (club fungi, e.g. Agaricus, rusts, smuts), Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi, no known sexual stage, e.g. Aspergillus, Candida).  ·  Body: mycelium (mass of hyphae); hyphae may be septate (divided) or coenocytic (aseptate).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Asexual & sexual reproduction  ·  Economic importance  ·  Decomposer role

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Basidiomycete spore: basidium (club) bearing basidiospores (4 typically)  ·  Economic roles: decomposers, food, medicine, industry; harmful: diseases, crop blights.  ·  Fungi ≠ plants: heterotrophic, chitin wall, absorptive nutrition.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Rhizopus (bread mould) is a Phycomycete; it reproduces by sporangiospores, not by sexual spores in the lab.  ·  Mushrooms (Agaricus) are Basidiomycetes; the visible mushroom is the fruiting body of the mycelium.  ·  Aspergillus niger → citric acid production, enzyme source (Deuteromycete).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The distinction between Ascomycetes (asci) and Basidiomycetes (basidia) is a common short-answer.  ·  Economic importance questions: give 3 beneficial and 3 harmful examples.  ·  Memorise the four fungal groups: name, spore type, example, one use.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Draw Penicillium and Rhizopus from memory.  ·  Learn the asexual vs sexual reproduction modes in fungi.  ·  List economic importance: food, medicine, industry, ecology, disease.
